data.one_liner: Cross-platform on-device LLM inference for Dart and Flutter.
data.what_it_does: Runs GGUF (llama.cpp) and LiteRT-LM models locally on Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, Linux, and web behind a unified Dart API. Supports streaming chat, structured JSON output, tool calling, embeddings, and multimodal inputs.
use_when: You need on-device LLM inference without depending on a cloud backend.
You want to run GGUF or LiteRT-LM models in a Dart or Flutter application.
avoid_when: Your application targets low-memory devices that cannot handle local model execution.
You prefer relying entirely on remote cloud APIs like OpenAI.
strengths: Supports multiple platforms including mobile, desktop, and web.
Provides streaming chat, tool calling, and multimodal capabilities.
Eliminates the need for a local C++ toolchain via build hooks.
weaknesses: Requires substantial local storage and memory for model files.
Web support is experimental and requires specific bridge assets setup.
data.setup_notes: Requires downloading or parsing model files, setting platform deployment targets (e.g., iOS 16.4+, macOS 14.0+), and adding native companion packages for Apple platforms.

alternatives.name: openai_dart
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want to use cloud-based OpenAI models instead of running models locally on-device.

alternatives.name: tflite_flutter
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you are specifically targeting TensorFlow Lite models for general machine learning tasks rather than LLMs.

alternatives.name: firebase_ai
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want to leverage Firebase-hosted AI capabilities instead of local on-device inference.
